subject: zenGarden
reasoning:
I'm picturing a stylized Japanese garden diorama sitting on a base: raked gravel, rocks, a stone lantern, a pruned pine, a small arched bridge, a koi pond, and bamboo stalks arranged together into a cohesive scene.

I'll keep the build robust by baking rotations and dimensions directly into the geometry rather than relying on uncertain SDK transform options, using simple box and cylinder primitives for the gravel base, sunken pond, stepping stones, and mounds, all sized in meters within roughly a 4x3 footprint and sticking to simple hex colors.

I'm now adding a wooden-framed border, a stone lantern, rock groupings, a low arched bridge over the pond made from cylinder segments, clustered bamboo canes, and a small teahouse with a stylized pyramid roof built from a rotated low-segment cone, while sketching out exact dimensions and placements for the gravel slab, wooden frame, and sunken water cylinder.

Now I'm placing scattered koi as flattened orange spheres on the water surface, grouping flattened dodecahedron rocks with mossy green caps, and building a pine tree with a tapered trunk and stacked, flattened pine-cloud foliage clusters. I'm also constructing the stone lantern from a base, pedestal, lantern body with a dark inset window, and a four-sided pyramid roof with a finial on top.

Next I'm adding a cluster of thin, slightly tilted bamboo stalks with darker node rings near the back-right corner, then building an arched taiko bridge over the pond using a half-torus oriented so its walkway spans across the water with ends resting at ground level on either side.

Scaling the arc down in height, I'm computing tangent angles along the ellipse to place individual plank boxes so each one rotates to stay aligned with the curve of the bridge as it rises and falls.

Now I'm adding stepping stones as flattened cylinders scattered near the gravel front, then designing a small back-left teahouse pavilion: a wooden platform, four corner posts, and a dark square pyramidal roof made from a scaled, rotated cylinder to mimic hip-roof pagoda styling.

I'm now laying out the full garden coordinate plan—pond, bridge, pine, bamboo, lantern, rocks, and stepping stones positioned across the 4x3 plot—then working out the gravel/water height relationships so the pond cylinder sits flush with the gravel slab surface.

I'm also figuring out the bridge geometry: an arched torus spanning the pond's diameter with its endpoints resting at the pond edges, oriented so viewers see the arch from the front, plus planning plank positions evenly spaced along the arc.

Each plank needs to be rotated to align with the tangent of the arc at its position, so I'm computing the tangent angle and using it to rotate a thin box shape (narrow along the path, wide across it) to sit correctly on the curve. I'm trusting that the `at` parameter in my helper function places geometry at the given coordinates, and keeping color usage within reasonable limits by using a shared material per color string.

For deterministic randomness I'm leaning toward skipping `rng()` uncertainty and just hand-coding jitter values for bamboo and rocks to keep things safe and predictable. I'm also deciding static scenery props don't need joints since they can ride directly off the root.

For the gravel, instead of a complex rake texture I'm planning simple concentric thin torus rings laid flat around the pond at slightly varying radii to suggest a raked pattern in a lighter color.

Now I'm working out the layout and placement of a stylized pine tree -- a flattened mound shape, a leaning trunk cylinder, and several flattened icosahedron foliage clusters at different heights with a dark green color, keeping everything low-poly, and checking that the rake rings and pine don't awkwardly overlap the pavilion or pond.

I'm designing a small stone lantern (tōrō): a layered base, pedestal, boxy lantern body with a dark window cutout, a flaring pyramidal roof made from a cylinder with mismatched top/bottom radii, and a small finial sphere on top, all stacked at consistent heights above ground level. Now I'm placing decorative rocks around the garden, starting with a larger scaled dodecahedron rock near the front right.

I'm scattering a second smaller rock nearby, adding a patch of flattened green moss on top, and laying stepping stones across the gravel path while checking their distance from the pond so none overlap it. Then I start building a bamboo cluster using five leaning cylindrical poles with slightly varied heights and rotations to simulate natural growth.

I'm adding darker green segment nodes along each pole for bamboo texture, then topping each one with a flattened leafy sphere, and now I'm beginning to lay out a pavilion structure with a wooden platform base.

Still designing pavilion geometry... I'm positioning the corner posts, back wall panel, and working out dimensions for a pyramidal roof using a scaled four-sided cylinder, aiming for the right width-to-height proportions before placing it atop the posts.

Now I'm working out tree placement using icosahedron foliage and a scaled sphere mound, then listing out the full color palette for gravel, water, rocks, moss, pine, lanterns, pavilion, and bridge elements. I'm placing koi as elongated ellipsoid spheres on the water surface with slight rotation variety, adding a lily pad cylinder, and moving on to planning the bridge.

For the bridge, I'm deciding to skip separate rail tori for simplicity and just use a single arched plank structure spanning the water, scaled and positioned so it reads as a stylized wooden footbridge without extra ornamentation.

I'm now working through precise spatial layout for each garden element to avoid overlaps—calculating plank counts and spacing along the bridge arc, mound and foliage positions for the leaning pine, and placement coordinates for rocks, lantern, stepping stones, bamboo cluster, and pavilion so nothing collides with the pond's circular footprint. I'm sketching out the TypeScript build function structure with helper utilities for placing geometry, then working through exact dimensions and vertical offsets for the gravel bed, pond, koi, lily pad, rocks with moss, and the stone lantern's base, pedestal, body, window, roof, and finial, adjusting heights so each piece sits correctly relative to the gravel surface. I'm also refining the pavilion's platform, posts, back wall, and pyramidal roof dimensions, and double-checking the raked sand rings and bridge arc geometry and texture colors for the finished scene.
